title: A heavier charge in a magnetic field
hook: Change particle mass and predict circular-orbit radius.
misconception: circular-orbit radius stays fixed when particle mass doubles.
objective: Apply r = mv/(abs(q)B) to compare circular-orbit radius when particle mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic charged particle at fixed speed and charge moving perpendicular to a fixed field, r = mv/(abs(q)B). When particle mass doubles, circular-orbit radius becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model r = mv/(abs(q)B); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic charged particle at fixed speed and charge moving perpendicular to a fixed field, with a nonzero initial result. If particle mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on circular-orbit radius?
recall.why: Apply r = mv/(abs(q)B) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
